## Summary

Fixed the New Epic modal's ambiguous "Type" picker by splitting it into two clearly-labeled, independent selections, matching what the reference screenshot was missing:

- **Agent** row (new) — a `<select>` populated from `window.api.agents.listPersonas()` (the same data behind the Agent Library tab), defaulting to "Default", with the persona's description shown alongside once picked.
- **Mission** row (renamed from "Type") — the existing Feature/Bug/Discussion pills, now labeled to match the Tag Library's own terminology and with a tooltip explaining it drives `/develop` eagerness.

Wired end-to-end, not just cosmetic:
- `PromptSession.agent?: string` (new field, `state/promptSessions.ts`) alongside the existing `tag`.
- `createPromptSession` takes an optional 5th `agent` arg; `NewEpicCard.tsx` passes it when a persona is chosen.
- `composeEpicIntake` (`lib/epicIntake.ts`) folds the chosen persona's name+description into `openingPrompt` as a framing line ahead of the mission's own grounding template — "who" before "what" — leaving `goalText` untouched.
- Updated `prompt-sessions/README.md`'s `PromptSession` shape and `CLAUDE.md`'s Epic domain-model section to document the two-axis model.
- Added/updated tests in `NewEpicCard.test.tsx` and `epicIntake.test.ts` covering the agent selector, its threading into `createPromptSession`, and the prompt framing.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, full `npm run test:unit` — 217 files / 2028 tests passing.

## Summary

Implemented the New Epic redesign from the Claude Design project (`Epics.html` / `variants/epic-new.jsx`), matching both attached screenshots.

**Front face** (`NewEpicCard.tsx`): two side-by-side columns — **"1 · Agent — who is working"** (a real button list from the Agent Library, with a hashed dot color per persona and a "Default" option) and **"2 · Mission — how they work"** (the existing feature/bug/discussion pills, with a grounding description that now also shows the selected persona's real tool list). An "advanced" toggle switch sits in the header next to the eyebrow.

**Back face** — a genuine 3D card-flip (CSS `rotateY`) reveals a **grounding board**: three columns (System/Project/Local) showing what this Epic's session will actually load — real global/project/local `CLAUDE.md` files (existence + line count), skills counts, MCP server names, hook counts, the project brief, the selected persona's own file (marked locked/required), git branch, open Terminal tabs in the project, and other Epics in the project. All of this is computed by a new `lib/groundingBoard.ts` from real `window.api.config.*` reads — no fabricated numbers. Since session-manager has no mechanism to make the `claude` CLI skip a file it would otherwise discover, the board is deliberately read-only (an inspector, not a control) rather than fake interactive toggles.

Also updated: `epicIntake.ts` unchanged from the prior turn (agent framing still folds into `openingPrompt`), test suites extended (`NewEpicCard.test.tsx` now covers the button-list agent picker and the flip interaction; new `groundingBoard.test.ts`), and `CLAUDE.md`'s Epic domain-model note extended to document the flip/grounding-board.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, full `npm run test:unit` — 218 files / 2033 tests passing.

Not done: actually launching the Electron app to visually confirm the flip animation/layout in a live window — this repo's memory notes that a second Ele…

Good — the final `agentType` rename is safely captured in the committed state. Everything is verified working and committed (by an automated hook I didn't invoke — flagging this below).

## Summary

Fixed two concrete drift bugs the previous pass introduced, so the New Epic card is now genuinely backed by the same global concepts session-manager already exposes elsewhere:

1. **Mission text was a third, drifted copy.** `NewEpicCard.tsx`'s Mission pills carried hand-authored blurb text lifted from the design mockup, diverging from both `lib/tagLibrary.ts`'s `TAG_LIBRARY` (the Tag Library page's own source) and `lib/agentTagDefs.ts`'s `AGENT_TAG_DEFS` (already the canonical "what this tag means" text, already used by `epicIntake.ts`'s grounding template). Fixed: the Mission blurb now reads through `agentTagDef(tag).description` at render time — one source, everywhere. Added a regression test (`shows the Mission blurb from the single global agentTagDef source, never a local copy`) that would fail if this drifts again. Updated `agentTagDefs.ts`'s doc comment to describe the new relationship.

2. **`PromptSession.agent` was a newly-invented field name for a concept that already has an established name in this app.** Claude Code's own `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` hook payloads use `agent_type`, the Task tool's own parameter is `subagent_type` (tracked as `subagentType` in `state/live.ts`), and a Team member's persona field in `teams.cjs` is `agentType`. Renamed `PromptSession.agent` → `agentType` (and `createPromptSession`'s 5th param to match) throughout `promptSessions.ts`, so the "which persona" concept carries the same name it already carries everywhere else in the codebase instead of a fourth synonym. Updated `prompt-sessions/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` accordingly.

The Agent side was already correctly sourced from the same global `window.api.agents.listPersonas()` API `AgentLibrary.tsx` uses — no drift there, confirmed by inspection.

Verified: `npm run typecheck`…

Committed as `218251c`. Working tree is now clean — this covered the remaining runtime state (active-index.json + the two Epic transcripts logging this conversation), since the actual code fix (the Agent/Mission API-sync pass: `agentType` rename, `agentTagDef`-sourced Mission text) was already captured in the earlier `1c8f5ed` commit. Not pushed to `origin/main` — say so if you want that too.

## Summary

Fixed the layout bug and widened the modal in `NewEpicCard.tsx`:

**Root cause of the overlap/off-ness**: the front/back faces toggled between `position: static` and `position: absolute` depending on `advanced`. Since only one face was ever "in flow" at a time, the container's height was driven by whichever face happened to be static — the instant you clicked the toggle, the layout height snapped to the *other* face's height before the 3D rotation even started animating, so the visible face got stretched/cropped against a height that belonged to the face flipping in. That read as overlapping/jumbled content mid-flip.

**Fix**: both faces are now permanently `position: absolute; inset: 0` inside a perspective box with a real fixed height (`min(760px, 84vh)`) — never toggled, so there's nothing to snap. Each face is a `flex flex-col` with its own header, a scrollable body (`flex-1 overflow-y-auto`), and a footer pinned to the bottom with a `border-t` divider — so long content (a big Agent Library, a wide grounding board) scrolls internally instead of stretching or clipping the card.

**Wider modal**: max-width went from a fixed 660px/860px to `min(920px, 92vw)` (front) / `min(1320px, 94vw)` (advanced/grounding board) — it now uses most of the available page width on typical windows instead of a narrow fixed column, while still capping sanely on very wide displays.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, full `npm run test:unit` — 218 files / 2034 tests passing (including the flip and grounding-board tests, unaffected by the layout change).

Not verified: the actual rendered flip animation in a live window — this is a one-shot headless run and launching a second Electron instance risks killing this repo's live scheduler jobs, so I could not visually confirm the fix beyond the DOM/CSS structure and passing tests.

## Summary

Committed as `680b286` (my verified NewEpicCard flip-layout fix, plus this Epic's own prompt-sessions transcript state).

Also saved a standing memory (`feedback_always_commit_after_verified_changes.md`) so this doesn't need to be repeated: going forward in this repo, I'll commit locally as soon as a change is verified (typecheck/tests green) rather than waiting to be asked each time. Push/publish still needs an explicit release trigger, per the existing publish-autonomy memory — this only covers the local commit step.

One thing worth flagging: `src/main/agentLibrary.cjs`, `src/main/index.cjs`, `src/preload/api.d.ts`, and `src/preload/index.cjs` are sitting modified in this working tree with real Agent Library CRUD work (`savePersona`/`deletePersona`/`removeOverride`) that I didn't write and haven't verified — it belongs to a different, apparently concurrent Epic session in this same repo. I deliberately left those unstaged rather than sweeping them into my commit. You may want to check on that session directly, since two agents editing the same tree concurrently is worth knowing about regardless of this task.

## Summary

Reviewed the other 3 open Epics in this repo to ground the language update in current reality, not guesswork:

1. **`/builder`** — routine release (v0.53.0→v0.54.0), unrelated to terminology.
2. **"Redesign Agent and Tag Library"** — the one directly relevant: it made `AgentLibrary.tsx` a full CRUD editor (New/Duplicate/Save/Revert/Delete, writing `~/.claude/agents/<name>.md`) and gave each persona a `tags:` frontmatter field, making agent↔tag membership editable from either the Agent Library or Tag Library page. Still in progress/uncommitted on disk (not mine to touch).
3. **"Project Home Redesign"** — bug fix running the Project Pages generate pipeline; unrelated to terminology.

**CLAUDE.md changes made** (docs only, no API/code changes, per your instruction):
- Added a short framing note under the domain-model header: **Agent** (persona, "who") + **Tag** (mission, "what") is the current UI vocabulary — explicitly *not* a rename of "Epic" or its underlying `PromptSession.agentType`/`tag` fields.
- Fixed the "New Epic creation is two independent selections" bullet, which still called `AgentLibrary.tsx`/`TagLibrary.tsx` "read-only directories" — stale as of the in-flight redesign. Now describes the real CRUD editor and the many-to-many agent↔tag membership.
- Replaced a stale "Knowledge Graph" mention in the intro tab list with "Agent Library, Tag Library" (KG was already retired per the Architecture section, replaced by Memory Clusters).
- Removed the dead "Knowledge graph data pipeline" convention bullet — it described a retired feature and directly contradicted the Architecture section in the same file.

Committed as `cf752fe` (only `CLAUDE.md` + this Epic's own transcript state — left the other Epic's uncommitted `agentLibrary.cjs`/`AgentLibrary.tsx`/etc. changes untouched, same isolation as before).

Pushed successfully — `origin/main` is now up to date, and even ahead of my own last commit.

## Summary

Ran `git push origin main`: my 4 pending local commits (New Epic card flip-fix, Project Home pipeline fix + Agent Library registration, and the CLAUDE.md language update) are now on `origin/main`. All existing tags were already in sync with the remote, so nothing else needed pushing there.

One thing worth flagging: right as I pushed, `origin/main` advanced one commit further to `a41c2f6` ("fix(epics): stop rendering assistant replies twice in Discussion") from a concurrent Epic session working in this same repo — then that session reset its local branch back one commit (visible in `git reflog`), which left its change unstaged in the shared working tree (that's the `EpicDetail.tsx`/`EpicDetail.test.tsx` and other modified files you'll see in `git status` right now). That's someone else's in-progress work being redone, not mine — I left it untouched, same as the other concurrent Agent/Tag Library CRUD changes from earlier. Your `origin/main` is current and contains everything I was asked to publish.

## Summary

Found and fixed the root cause of the New Epic card's front-tile bug (matching the designer reference in image 2 vs. the garbled live app in image 1).

**Root cause**: each agent row was a flex button with `<dot> <name> <description className="ml-auto truncate whitespace-nowrap">`. Flex children default to `min-width: auto`, so `truncate` silently did nothing on the description span — it never shrinks below its own content width. My tests only used short mock persona names/descriptions, so this never surfaced there, but a real persona like `project-home-builder` (a full-sentence description) blew the row's width out sideways, dragging the whole two-column Agent/Mission grid with it — exactly what your screenshot shows: garbled layout with a horizontal scrollbar cutting off the left side of each row.

**Fix** in `NewEpicCard.tsx`:
- Threaded `min-w-0` down through every ancestor (grid item → row list → button) — `truncate` only works if every flex/grid ancestor between it and its container allows shrinking.
- Gave the dot and name `flex-shrink-0` so they're never compressed.
- Changed the description span from `ml-auto truncate whitespace-nowrap` to `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate` — it now correctly claims exactly the remaining row width and ellipsizes.
- Added `overflow-x-hidden` next to the existing `overflow-y-auto` on both scrollable card bodies (front and grounding-board back) — per the CSS spec, `overflow-y-auto` alone silently promotes `overflow-x` to `auto` too, which is what revealed the horizontal scrollbar in the first place.
- Added a regression test using a real persona-length description (`project-home-builder`'s actual sentence) to catch this specific failure mode going forward — the short test fixtures used elsewhere in the file wouldn't have caught it.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors` clean, full `npm run test:unit` — 219 files / 2046 tests passing. Committed as `e8e2b0e` (only my files — left the other concurren…

Checked directly rather than assuming:

**Yes — both of my New Epic card fixes are in v0.55.1:**
- `e8e2b0e` (stop the agent row from overflowing sideways)
- `df3b604` (the typecheck follow-up fixing the test fixture)

Confirmed via `git merge-base --is-ancestor e8e2b0e v0.55.1` → yes, and `git log v0.55.0..v0.55.1` shows both commits in that range.

One thing worth flagging though: **v0.55.1 isn't actually live anywhere yet.**
- `origin/main` on GitHub is still at `80bb5cc` (v0.55.0-era) — the v0.55.1 tag/bump commit exists only locally, not pushed.
- `npm view claude-code-session-manager dist-tags` still shows `latest: 0.55.0`.
- The v0.55.1 tag commit (`162ff31`) isn't reachable from any local or remote branch — it looks like it was cut in an isolated worktree (per this repo's own publish convention) whose branch never got fast-forwarded/pushed back to `main`, or the publish sequence stopped partway through.

So: my changes are correctly included in the v0.55.1 cut, but that cut hasn't reached GitHub or npm yet — worth checking on whichever concurrent `/builder` run did this if you expected it to be live already.

/**

 * session-manager-operations/design-mocks/epics/DESIGN_SPEC.md §"New Epic card".

  onCreated,

  const activeTabCwd = useSessions((s) => s.tabs.find((t) => t.id === s.activeTabId)?.cwd ?? null)

  const knownCwds = useMemo(() => {

  const att = useAttachments()
  const [creating, setCreating] = useState(false)

    setCwd('')

    setGoal('')
    setTag('feature')
    att.clear()

    if (!canCreate || creating) return

        <p className="my-2 mb-[18px] text-[13.5px] leading-[1.55] text-fg-dim">

        {showProjectSelector ? (

            <span className="font-mono text-[10.5px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.09em] text-fg-faint">
              Project
            </span>
            <select
              data-testid="new-prompt-cwd"
              value={effectiveCwd}
              onChange={(e) => setCwd(e.target.value)}
              className="rounded-md border border-line bg-bg px-2 py-1.5 font-mono text-[12.5px] text-fg"

              {knownCwds.length === 0 && <option value="">No known projects</option>}
              {knownCwds.map((c) => (

            >

      </div>
    </section>
  )

import { Panel } from '../ui/Panel'
import { ListDetail } from '../ui/ListDetail'
import { EmptyState } from '../ui/EmptyState'
import { toast } from '../../state/toast'
import type { AgentPersona } from '../../../preload/api'

/**
 * Agent Library — read-only directory of agent personas. Follows Skills.tsx's
 * canonical list+detail shape: a component-local fetch on mount (no store,
 * since this data isn't hot/live), a filterable sidebar list, and a detail
 * pane for the selected item. Home face only — this is cross-project/machine
 * data, not a per-project view (see navGroups.ts).
 *
 * Global personas come from `~/.claude/agents/*.md`; `overridingProjects`
 * lists which currently-open project tabs have a same-named overlay at
 * `<cwd>/.claude/agents/<name>.md`, which Claude Code's own precedence rules
 * prefer over the global definition.
 */
export function AgentLibrary() {
  const [personas, setPersonas] = useState<AgentPersona[] | null>(null)
  const [selectedName, setSelectedName] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState('')
  const mounted = useRef(true)
  useEffect(() => () => { mounted.current = false }, [])

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false
    ;(async () => {
      try {
        const list = await window.api.agents.listPersonas()
        if (cancelled || !mounted.current) return
        setPersonas(list)
        setSelectedName((cur) => cur ?? list[0]?.name ?? null)
      } catch (e) {
        if (cancelled || !mounted.current) return
        setPersonas([])
        toast.error((e as Error).message || 'failed to load agent personas')
      }
    })()
    return () => { cancelled = true }
  }, [])

  if (personas === null) return <EmptyState title="loading…" />

  const needle = filter.toLowerCase()
  const filtered = personas.filter(
    (p) => !needle || p.name.toLowerCase().includes(needle) || (p.description ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(needle),
  )
  const selected = personas.find((p) => p.name === selectedName) ?? null

  return (
    <Panel
      toolbar={
        <>
          <span className="text-fg-faint">
            {personas.length} persona{personas.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}
          </span>
          <div className="flex-1" />
          {selected && <span className="text-fg-faint truncate">{selected.path}</span>}
        </>
      }
    >
      <ListDetail
        sidebar={
          <div className="py-1">
            <div className="px-2 pb-1">
              <input
                value={filter}
                onChange={(e) => setFilter(e.target.value)}
                placeholder="filter…"
                className="w-full bg-bg border border-line rounded px-2 py-0.5 text-xs text-fg"
              />
            </div>
            {filtered.length === 0 ? (
              <div className="px-3 py-1 text-xs text-fg-faint italic">no agent personas found</div>
            ) : (
              filtered.map((p) => (
                <button
                  key={p.name}
                  onClick={() => setSelectedName(p.name)}
                  className={`w-full text-left px-3 py-1 text-xs flex flex-col gap-0.5 ${
                    selectedName === p.name
                      ? 'bg-bg-hi text-fg'
                      : 'text-fg-dim hover:text-fg hover:bg-bg-hi'
                  }`}
                >
                  <span className="flex items-center gap-2 justify-between w-full">
                    <span className="truncate">{p.name}</span>
                    {p.overridingProjects.length > 0 && (
                      <span
                        className="shrink-0 px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] rounded border border-line text-fg-faint"
                        title={`Overridden in: ${p.overridingProjects.join(', ')}`}
                      >
                        {p.overridingProjects.length} override{p.overridingProjects.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}
                      </span>
                    )}
                  </span>
                  {p.description && (
                    <span className="truncate text-fg-faint">{p.description}</span>
                  )}
                </button>
              ))
            )}
          </div>
        }
        detail={selected ? <AgentPersonaDetail persona={selected} /> : <EmptyState title="select an agent" />}
      />
    </Panel>
  )
}

function AgentPersonaDetail({ persona }: { persona: AgentPersona }) {
  return (
    <div className="p-4 space-y-4 max-w-3xl">
      <div>
        <div className="text-sm font-semibold text-fg">{persona.name}</div>
        {persona.description && <div className="text-xs text-fg-dim mt-1">{persona.description}</div>}
      </div>
      <div>
        <div className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-fg-faint mb-1">Tools</div>
        {persona.tools.length > 0 ? (
          <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">
            {persona.tools.map((t) => (
              <span key={t} className="px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] rounded border border-line text-fg-dim font-mono">
                {t}
              </span>
            ))}
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div className="text-xs text-fg-faint italic">no tools restriction declared</div>
        )}
      </div>
      <div>
        <div className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-fg-faint mb-1">Overriding projects</div>
        {persona.overridingProjects.length > 0 ? (
          <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">
            {persona.overridingProjects.map((name) => (
              <span key={name} className="px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] rounded border border-line text-fg-faint">
                {name}
              </span>
            ))}
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div className="text-xs text-fg-faint italic">
            no open project overlays this agent — the global definition applies everywhere
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
      <div>
        <div className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wider text-fg-faint mb-1">Definition</div>
        <pre className="text-xs text-fg-dim whitespace-pre-wrap bg-bg-elev border border-line rounded p-3 max-h-[50vh] overflow-auto">
          {persona.body}
        </pre>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

346	/**
347	 * Enqueue a chat run for a tab. Fire-and-forget — results arrive via IPC.
348	 * Both silent (automated probe) and manual (user-initiated) runs share the
349	 * CONCURRENCY_CAP=2 (default) FIFO lane — extra submits queue and are
350	 * announced via chat:run:queued (silent runs stay invisible to the renderer;
351	 * see pump() below). De-dupes a tab already in the pipeline (the renderer's
352	 * per-tab prompt queue in chat.ts only ever calls this once per tab at a
353	 * time, but the guard holds regardless).
354	 *
355	 * @param {{ tabId: string, sessionId: string, prompt: string, cwd: string, resume: boolean, silent?: boolean, onSilentResult?: (text: string) => void, promptId?: string }} opts
356	 */
357	function run(opts) {
358	  // Per-tab exclusivity still holds — two `claude -p --resume` against ONE
359	  // sessionId must never overlap — but it is now enforced in pump() (which
360	  // refuses to start a run for a tab that already has one live) rather than by
361	  // discarding the submission here.
362	  //
363	  // Dropping was silent and unrecoverable: `chat:run` still resolved
364	  // { ok: true }, so the renderer sat at running: true forever with no toast
365	  // and no terminal event. A `silent` /context probe holding the tabId was
366	  // enough to swallow a user's message. User-initiated sends are now QUEUED
367	  // behind whatever holds the tab and dispatched in FIFO order.
368	  // `dispatching` counts as busy too: between pump() picking a run and
369	  // executeRun registering it in `inFlight`, the tab is committed but not yet
370	  // visible in `inFlight` — the same window pump() guards against.
371	  const tabBusy = inFlight.has(opts.tabId)
372	    || dispatching.has(opts.tabId)
373	    || waiting.some((w) => w.tabId === opts.tabId);
374	  if (tabBusy && opts.silent) {
375	    // Silent probes stay best-effort and invisible: a probe that collides is
376	    // still dropped, since queueing one would delay real work to no benefit.
377	    return { accepted: false, reason: 'tab-busy-silent' };
378	  }
379	
380	  waiting.push(opts);
381	  pump();
382	  return { accepted: true, queued: tabBusy };
383	}
384	
385	// Fill open lanes FIFO up to CONCURRENCY_CAP, then announce queue positions for
386	// the remainder. O(n) over the waiting list (bounded by open tabs).
387	function pump() {
388	  while (activeCount < getConcurrencyCap() && waiting.length > 0) {
389	    // Per-tab exclusivity: skip past any waiting run whose tab already has one
390	    // live, rather than head-blocking the whole lane on it. `dispatching`
391	    // covers the gap between picking a job here and executeRun() registering
392	    // it in `inFlight` (which happens a microtask later) — without it, one
393	    // synchronous sweep of this loop could start two runs for the same tab and
394	    // race two --resume processes against a single sessionId.
395	    const idx = waiting.findIndex((w) => !inFlight.has(w.tabId) && !dispatching.has(w.tabId));
396	    // Everything queued is blocked behind its own tab's live run; the settle()
397	    // of that run re-pumps.
398	    if (idx === -1) break;
399	    // The chat lane cap is a POLICY bound; actual capacity comes from the
400	    // Session-Manager-wide slot pool shared with the scheduler
401	    // (lib/sessionSlots.cjs). No slot → everyone keeps waiting; the next
402	    // settle() in either subsystem re-pumps.
403	    const slotToken = sessionSlots.acquire(`chat:${waiting[idx].tabId}`);
404	    if (!slotToken) break;
405	    const [job] = waiting.splice(idx, 1);
406	    activeCount += 1;
407	    dispatching.add(job.tabId);
408	    Promise.resolve()
409	      .then(() => {
410	        const donePromise = executor(job);
411	        const entry = inFlight.get(job.tabId);
412	        if (entry) entry.donePromise = donePromise;
413	        return donePromise;
414	      })
415	      .catch(() => { /* executeRun never rejects; defensive */ })
416	      .finally(() => {
417	        dispatching.delete(job.tabId);
418	        sessionSlots.release(slotToken);
419	        activeCount -= 1;
420	        pump();
421	      });
422	  }
423	  // Anyone still waiting gets a 1-based position update. Silent (automated
424	  // probe) runs must stay invisible to the renderer, same as every other
425	  // broadcast in executeRun — otherwise a queued probe would flip a tab's
426	  // `running`/`queuedPosition` UI state for a run the user never initiated.
427	  waiting.forEach((w, i) => {
428	    if (w.silent) return;
429	    broadcast('chat:run:queued', { tabId: w.tabId, sessionId: w.sessionId, position: i + 1 });
430	  });
431	}
432	
433	// A slot freed anywhere (e.g. a scheduler job settled) may unblock our lane.
434	sessionSlots.subscribe(() => { try { pump(); } catch { /* defensive */ } });

438	/**

448	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
449	    const startedAt = Date.now();
450	    // Last few tool_use blocks seen on the stream, oldest first — surfaced in

453	    let settled = false;
454	    // Frees the lane exactly once: drops the cancel fn and resolves the promise
455	    // the pump is awaiting. Both exit and error paths funnel through here.
456	    const settle = () => {
457	      if (settled) return;
458	      settled = true;
459	      inFlight.delete(tabId);
460	      resolve();
461	    };
462	
463	    // Guarantees the renderer receives EXACTLY ONE terminal event
464	    // (complete / needs-input / error) per run. Without this, a cancelled or

470	    let terminalSent = false;
471	    const emitTerminal = (channel, payload) => {
472	      if (terminalSent) return;
473	      terminalSent = true;

 * Epic needs, from one source so they can never disagree:

 *                       what they just entered.
 *
 * The title is the session's GOAL; the sub-header (goal field) is the FIRST
 * INSTRUCTION. References are appended as trailing lines to both.
 */

import { agentTagDef } from './agentTagDefs'
import type { TicketTag } from './ticketDisplay'

export interface EpicIntakeFields {
  /** Epic title — optional; becomes the session's goal line. */
  title: string
  /** The objective / first instruction. Required (the form gates on it). */
  goal: string
  /** Absolute paths of attached references. */
  referencePaths?: string[]
  /**
   * The Epic's single tag. When given, its `initialPromptTemplate`
   * (agentTagDefs.ts) is prepended to `openingPrompt` only — `goalText`
   * stays the pure user objective, since that's what's displayed as the
   * Epic's identity in Scheduler chips / the composer header.
   */
  tag?: TicketTag
}

export interface EpicIntake {
  goalText: string
  openingPrompt: string
}

/** File names are user/filesystem controlled and can contain newlines — strip
 *  them so a crafted name can't forge an extra structural line. */
function singleLine(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ')
}

function withReferences(body: string, referencePaths: string[]): string {
  const lines = referencePaths.map((p) => `Reference: ${singleLine(p)}`)
  return lines.length ? `${body}\n\n${lines.join('\n')}` : body
}

/**
 * Compose an Epic's stored `goalText` and its auto-sent opening prompt.
 *
 * Complexity: O(n) in the number of references.
 */
export function composeEpicIntake({ title, goal, referencePaths = [], tag }: EpicIntakeFields): EpicIntake {
  const trimmedTitle = singleLine(title.trim())
  const trimmedGoal = goal.trim()

  const body = trimmedTitle ? `${trimmedTitle}\n\n${trimmedGoal}` : trimmedGoal
  // The opening prompt names the title as the goal explicitly, so the agent
  // reads it as the objective rather than as the first line of the request.
  const promptBody = trimmedTitle ? `Goal: ${trimmedTitle}\n\n${trimmedGoal}` : trimmedGoal
  // The tag's grounding template comes first — it's the agent's framing
  // instruction, read before the human's own goal.
  const groundedPromptBody = tag ? `${agentTagDef(tag).initialPromptTemplate}\n\n${promptBody}` : promptBody

  return {
    goalText: withReferences(body, referencePaths),
    openingPrompt: withReferences(groundedPromptBody, referencePaths),
  }
}

   *  to run this Epic, distinct from `tag` above. When given along with
   *  `agentDescription`, a framing line names the persona before the tag's

}","originalFile":"/**
 * epicIntake — turns the New Epic form's fields into the two strings a new
 * Epic needs, from one source so they can never disagree:
 *
 *   - `goalText`      — the Epic's stored identity (what the queue, Scheduler
 *                       chips and composer header display).
 *   - `openingPrompt` — the first message sent into the Epic's claude session
 *                       automatically at creation, so the Epic opens already
 *                       waiting on the agent instead of on the user retyping
 *                       what they just entered.
 *
 * The title is the session's GOAL; the sub-header (goal field) is the FIRST
 * INSTRUCTION. References are appended as trailing lines to both.
 */

import { agentTagDef } from './agentTagDefs'
import type { TicketTag } from './ticketDisplay'

export interface EpicIntakeFields {
  /** Epic title — optional; becomes the session's goal line. */
  title: string
  /** The objective / first instruction. Required (the form gates on it). */
  goal: string
  /** Absolute paths of attached references. */
  referencePaths?: string[]
  /**
   * The Epic's single tag. When given, its `initialPromptTemplate`
   * (agentTagDefs.ts) is prepended to `openingPrompt` only — `goalText`
   * stays the pure user objective, since that's what's displayed as the
   * Epic's identity in Scheduler chips / the composer header.
   */
  tag?: TicketTag
}

export interface EpicIntake {
  goalText: string
  openingPrompt: string
}

/** File names are user/filesystem controlled and can contain newlines — strip
 *  them so a crafted name can't forge an extra structural line. */
function singleLine(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ')
}

function withReferences(body: string, referencePaths: string[]): string {
  const lines = referencePaths.map((p) => `Reference: ${singleLine(p)}`)
  return lines.length ? `${body}\n\n${lines.join('\n')}` : body
}

/**
 * Compose an Epic's stored `goalText` and its auto-sent opening prompt.
 *
 * Complexity: O(n) in the number of references.
 */
export function composeEpicIntake({ title, goal, referencePaths = [], tag }: EpicIntakeFields): EpicIntake {
  const trimmedTitle = singleLine(title.trim())
  const trimmedGoal = goal.trim()

 * epicIntake — turns the New Epic form's fields into the two strings a new
 * Epic needs, from one source so they can never disagree:
 *
 *   - `goalText`      — the Epic's stored identity (what the queue, Scheduler
 *                       chips and composer header display).
 *   - `openingPrompt` — the first message sent into the Epic's claude session
 *                       automatically at creation, so the Epic opens already
 *                       waiting on the agent instead of on the user retyping
 *                       what they just entered.
 *
 * The title is the session's GOAL; the sub-header (goal field) is the FIRST
 * INSTRUCTION. References are appended as trailing lines to both.
 */

import { agentTagDef } from './agentTagDefs'
import type { TicketTag } from './ticketDisplay'

export interface EpicIntakeFields {
  /** Epic title — optional; becomes the session's goal line. */
  title: string
  /** The objective / first instruction. Required (the form gates on it). */
  goal: string
  /** Absolute paths of attached references. */
  referencePaths?: string[]
  /**
   * The Epic's single mission tag. When given, its `initialPromptTemplate`
   * (agentTagDefs.ts) is prepended to `openingPrompt` only — `goalText`
   * stays the pure user objective, since that's what's displayed as the
   * Epic's identity in Scheduler chips / the composer header.
   */
  tag?: TicketTag
  /** Name of the Agent Library persona (`~/.claude/agents/<name>.md`) chosen
   *  to run this Epic, distinct from `tag` above. When given along with
   *  `agentDescription`, a framing line names the persona before the tag's
   *  mission template — the persona is the "who", the tag is the "what". */
  agentName?: string
  /** The persona's one-line description (AgentPersona.description), shown
   *  alongside `agentName` in the framing line. Omitted from the framing
   *  line entirely when either is absent. */
  agentDescription?: string
}

export interface EpicIntake {
  goalText: string
  openingPrompt: string
}

/** File names are user/filesystem controlled and can contain newlines — strip
 *  them so a crafted name can't forge an extra structural line. */
function singleLine(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ')
}

function withReferences(body: string, referencePaths: string[]): string {
  const lines = referencePaths.map((p) => `Reference: ${singleLine(p)}`)
  return lines.length ? `${body}\n\n${lines.join('\n')}` : body
}

/**
 * Compose an Epic's stored `goalText` and its auto-sent opening prompt.
 *
 * Complexity: O(n) in the number of references.
 */
export function composeEpicIntake({ title, goal, referencePaths = [], tag }: EpicIntakeFields): EpicIntake {
  const trimmedTitle = singleLine(title.trim())
  const trimmedGoal = goal.trim()

  const body = trimmedTitle ? `${trimmedTitle}\n\n${trimmedGoal}` : trimmedGoal
  // The opening prompt names the title as the goal explicitly, so the agent
  // reads it as the objective rather than as the first line of the request.
  const promptBody = trimmedTitle ? `Goal: ${trimmedTitle}\n\n${trimmedGoal}` : trimmedGoal
  // The tag's grounding template comes first — it's the agent's framing
  // instruction, read before the human's own goal.
  const groundedPromptBody = tag ? `${agentTagDef(tag).initialPromptTemplate}\n\n${promptBody}` : promptBody

  return {
    goalText: withReferences(body, referencePaths),
    openingPrompt: withReferences(groundedPromptBody, referencePaths),
  }
}

  // Epics are always created from within a tab's project context — the
  // selector only earns its place on screen when that context is missing
  // (no active tab, or its cwd isn't a known project). Otherwise it's a
  // second way to change something already decided by which tab is open.
  const showProjectSelector = !(activeTabCwd && knownCwds.includes(activeTabCwd))

  const resetForm = () => {
    setCwd('')
    setTitle('')
    setGoal('')
    setTag('feature')
    setAgentName('')
    att.clear()
  }

  const handleCreate = async () => {
    if (!canCreate || creating) return
    setCreating(true)
    try {
    // goalText and the opening prompt come from one composer (lib/epicIntake)
    // so the Epic's stored identity and the message the agent actually reads
    // can't drift. Both are written exactly once: an Epic's title/objective
    // are fixed for the life of its session by design — iteration happens in
    // follow-up messages, not by rewriting the goal.
    // Pasted-clipboard images have no filesystem path until they are saved,
    // so resolve every attachment to a real path BEFORE folding it into the
    // goal text — otherwise the reference line names a file that never
    // existed (PRD 865).
    const referencePaths = await resolveAttachmentPaths(att.items, effectiveCwd)
    const { goalText, openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({
      title,
      goal,
      referencePaths,
      tag,
      agentName: selectedAgent?.name,
      agentDescription: selectedAgent?.description ?? undefined,
    })
    // Every Epic is BORN 'proposed'; nothing is created directly as 'active'.
    // Submitting this form is not a second kind of creation — it is the one
    // 'proposed -> active' transition, the same one EpicApprovalBar's
    // Approve & start takes. createPromptSession can only ever mint
    // 'proposed', so this call and the approveProposed below are what perform
    // that transition.
    // See prompt-sessions/README.md#lifecycle.
    const session = selectedAgent
      ? createPromptSession(effectiveCwd, goalText, tag, 'NewEpicCard', selectedAgent.name)
      : createPromptSession(effectiveCwd, goalText, tag, 'NewEpicCard')
    approveProposed(session.id, 'NewEpicCard')
    // Send the objective straight into the Epic's session, so it opens already
    // waiting on the agent — the user has just typed the goal, there is
    // nothing further for them to enter. Chat (not PRD dispatch) on purpose:
    // the first turn is the agent's response, which the user then acts on.
    useChat.getState().send({
      tabId: session.id,
      sessionId: session.claudeSessionId,
      cwd: effectiveCwd,
      prompt: openingPrompt,
    })
    resetForm()
    onCreated(session.id)
    } finally {
      setCreating(false)
    }
  }

  const handleCancel = () => {
    resetForm()
    onCancel()
  }

  return (
    <section className="flex-1 min-w-0 grid place-items-center overflow-y-auto bg-bg p-8" data-testid="new-epic-card">
      <div className="w-full max-w-[620px] rounded-2xl border border-line bg-bg-hi px-[26px] pb-[22px] pt-6">
        <div className="mb-1.5 font-mono text-[10.5px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.11em] text-accent">
          New Epic
        </div>
        <h2 className="m-0 font-serif text-2xl font-semibold tracking-[-0.3px] text-fg">
          What are we trying to achieve?
        </h2>
        <p className="my-2 mb-[18px] text-[13.5px] leading-[1.55] text-fg-dim">
          One goal per Epic — fixed for the life of its session. The title and objective are sent
          as the first message the moment you start it, so the agent is already working when it opens.
        </p>

        {showProjectSelector ? (
          <label className="mb-2.5 flex flex-col gap-1">
            <span className="font-mono text-[10.5px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.09em] text-fg-faint">
              Project
            </span>
            <select
              data-testid="new-prompt-cwd"
              value={effectiveCwd}
              onChange={(e) => setCwd(e.target.value)}
              className="rounded-md border border-line bg-bg px-2 py-1.5 font-mono text-[12.5px] text-fg"
            >
              {knownCwds.length === 0 && <option value="">No known projects</option>}
              {knownCwds.map((c) => (
                <option key={c} value={c}>{compactPath(c)}</option>
              ))}
            </select>
          </label>
        ) : (
          <div
            data-testid="new-prompt-cwd-static"
            className="mb-2.5 flex items-center gap-1.5 font-mono text-[11px] text-fg-faint"
          >
            <span className="uppercase tracking-[0.09em]">Project</span>
            <span className="text-fg-dim">{compactPath(effectiveCwd)}</span>
          </div>
        )}

        <input
          data-testid="new-epic-title"
          type="text"
          value={title}
          onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)}
          onPaste={(e) => attachPastedFiles(e, att)}
          placeholder="Epic title"
          className="mb-2 w-full appearance-none rounded-[10px] border border-line bg-bg px-[13px] py-[11px] text-sm font-semibold text-fg outline-none"
        />
        <textarea
          data-testid="new-epic-goal"
          rows={3}
          value={goal}
          onChange={(e) => setGoal(e.target.value)}
          onPaste={(e) => attachPastedFiles(e, att)}
          placeholder="The objective, in a sentence or two — this is sent as the first instruction."
          className="mb-3 w-full resize-y appearance-none rounded-[10px] border border-line bg-bg px-[13px] py-[11px] text-[13px] leading-[1.55] text-fg outline-none"
        />

        <div className="mb-1.5 font-mono text-[10.5px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.09em] text-fg-faint">
          references{att.items.length ? ` · ${att.items.length}` : ''}
        </div>
        <AttachTray att={att} tall testId="new-epic-attach-tray" />

        <div className="mt-4 flex items-center gap-2.5">
          <span
            className="font-mono text-[10.5px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.09em] text-fg-faint"
            title="Who runs this Epic — from the Agent Library (~/.claude/agents)."
          >
            agent
          </span>
          <select
            data-testid="new-epic-agent-select"
            value={agentName}
            onChange={(e) => setAgentName(e.target.value)}
            className="rounded-md border border-line bg-bg px-2 py-1 text-xs text-fg"
          >
            <option value="">Default</option>
            {(agents ?? []).map((a) => (
              <option key={a.name} value={a.name}>{a.name}</option>
            ))}
          </select>
          {selectedAgent?.description && (
            <span className="truncate text-[11px] text-fg-faint" title={selectedAgent.description}>
              {selectedAgent.description}
            </span>
          )}
        </div>

        <div className="mt-2.5 flex items-center gap-2.5">
          <span
            className="font-mono text-[10.5px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.09em] text-fg-faint"
            title="The Epic's mission — from the Tag Library. Sets how eagerly /develop fires."
          >
            mission
          </span>
          <span className="flex gap-0.5">
            {KIND_OPTIONS.map((opt) => {
              const on = tag === opt.tag
              return (
                <button
                  key={opt.tag}
                  type="button"
                  data-testid={`new-epic-kind-${opt.tag}`}
                  onClick={() => setTag(opt.tag)}
                  className={`rounded-md px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-medium ${
                    on ? 'bg-bg text-fg ring-1 ring-inset ring-line font-semibold' : 'text-fg-faint'
                  }`}
                >
                  {opt.label}
                </button>
              )
            })}
          </span>
          <span className="ml-auto flex gap-1.5">
            <button
              type="button"
              data-testid="new-epic-cancel"
              onClick={handleCancel}
              className="rounded-md border border-line bg-bg px-3.5 py-2 text-[12.5px] font-semibold text-fg-dim hover:bg-bg-elev"
            >
              Cancel
            </button>
            <button
              type="button"
              data-testid="new-epic-create"
              onClick={() => void handleCreate()}
              disabled={!canCreate || creating}
              className="rounded-md bg-accent px-4 py-2 text-[12.5px] font-semibold text-bg-hi disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-40"
            >
              {creating ? 'Starting…' : 'Start Epic'}
            </button>
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  )
}

import { describe, it, expect, afterEach, beforeEach, vi } from 'vitest'

import type { AgentPersona } from '../../../../preload/api'

const createPromptSessionSpy = vi.fn(usePromptSessions.getState().createPromptSession)
const sendSpy = vi.fn()
const listPersonasSpy = vi.fn<[], Promise<AgentPersona[]>>().mockResolvedValue([])

vi.mock('../../../lib/useKnownProjects', () => ({
  useKnownProjects: () => ({
    rows: [
      { encoded: '-home-bilko-Projects-alpha', displayPath: '', sessionCount: 0, lastSession: 0, path: '', sizeBytes: 0 },
      { encoded: '-home-bilko-Projects-beta', displayPath: '', sessionCount: 0, lastSession: 0, path: '', sizeBytes: 0 },
    ],
    enriched: {
      '-home-bilko-Projects-alpha': { cwd: '/home/bilko/Projects/alpha' },
      '-home-bilko-Projects-beta': { cwd: '/home/bilko/Projects/beta' },
    },
    loading: false,
  }),
  candidatePath: (encoded: string) => encoded.replace(/-/g, '/'),
}))

let container: HTMLDivElement | null = null
let root: Root | null = null

function mount(el: React.ReactElement) {
  container = document.createElement('div')
  document.body.appendChild(container)
  root = createRoot(container)
  act(() => root!.render(el))
  return container
}

function setNativeValue(el: HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement, value: string) {
  const proto = el instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement ? window.HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype : window.HTMLInputElement.prototype
  const setter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(proto, 'value')!.set!
  setter.call(el, value)
  el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }))
}

beforeEach(() => {
  usePromptSessions.setState({ sessions: {}, events: {} })
  usePromptSessions.setState({ createPromptSession: createPromptSessionSpy })
  createPromptSessionSpy.mockClear()
  useChat.setState({ send: sendSpy })
  sendSpy.mockClear()
  useSessions.setState({ tabs: [], activeTabId: null })
})

afterEach(() => {
  act(() => root?.unmount())
  container?.remove()
  container = null
  root = null
})

describe('NewEpicCard', () => {
  it('disables Create until a project and a goal are present', () => {
    const el = mount(<NewEpicCard onCreated={vi.fn()} onCancel={vi.fn()} />)
    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    expect(create.disabled).toBe(true)

    const goal = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-goal"]') as HTMLTextAreaElement
    act(() => setNativeValue(goal, 'Ship the thing'))
    expect(create.disabled).toBe(false)
  })

  it('calls createPromptSession(cwd, goal, tag) and fires onCreated with the new id on goal-only submission', async () => {
    const onCreated = vi.fn()
    const el = mount(<NewEpicCard onCreated={onCreated} onCancel={vi.fn()} />)

    const cwdSelect = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-prompt-cwd"]') as HTMLSelectElement
    act(() => {
      cwdSelect.value = '/home/bilko/Projects/beta'
      cwdSelect.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }))
    })
    const goal = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-goal"]') as HTMLTextAreaElement
    act(() => setNativeValue(goal, 'Fix the flaky test'))

    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => create.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    // handleCreate awaits attachment resolution (PRD 865) — flush it.
    await act(async () => {})

    expect(createPromptSessionSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/home/bilko/Projects/beta', 'Fix the flaky test', 'feature', 'NewEpicCard')
    const created = Object.values(usePromptSessions.getState().sessions)[0]
    expect(onCreated).toHaveBeenCalledWith(created.id)
  })

  it('folds a typed title in as a leading line and respects the selected kind pill', async () => {
    const onCreated = vi.fn()
    const el = mount(<NewEpicCard onCreated={onCreated} onCancel={vi.fn()} />)

    const title = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-title"]') as HTMLInputElement
    act(() => setNativeValue(title, 'Flaky test'))

    act(() => bugPill.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))

    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => create.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    // handleCreate awaits attachment resolution (PRD 865) — flush it.
    await act(async () => {})

    expect(createPromptSessionSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(

      'Flaky test\n\nMake CI stop flaking',
      'bug',
      'NewEpicCard',
    )
  })

  it('folds attached reference paths into goalText as trailing "Reference:" lines', async () => {
    const onCreated = vi.fn()
    const el = mount(<NewEpicCard onCreated={onCreated} onCancel={vi.fn()} />)

    const goal = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-goal"]') as HTMLTextAreaElement

    Object.defineProperty(file, 'path', { value: '/home/bilko/Downloads/crash.log' })
    Object.defineProperty(fileInput, 'files', { value: [file] })
    act(() => fileInput.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })))

    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => create.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    // handleCreate awaits attachment resolution (PRD 865) — flush it.
    await act(async () => {})

    expect(createPromptSessionSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      '/home/bilko/Projects/alpha',
      'Investigate the crash\n\nReference: /home/bilko/Downloads/crash.log',
      'feature',
      'NewEpicCard',
    )
  })

  it('resets form state after a successful create and on Cancel', async () => {
    const onCreated = vi.fn()
    const onCancel = vi.fn()

    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => create.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    // handleCreate awaits attachment resolution (PRD 865) — flush it.
    await act(async () => {})
    expect((el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-goal"]') as HTMLTextAreaElement).value).toBe('')

    act(() => setNativeValue(el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-goal"]') as HTMLTextAreaElement, 'another goal'))
    const cancel = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-cancel"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => cancel.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    expect(onCancel).toHaveBeenCalled()
    expect((el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-goal"]') as HTMLTextAreaElement).value).toBe('')
  })

  it('auto-sends the title + objective as the Epic\'s first prompt, so it opens waiting on the agent', async () => {
    const el = mount(<NewEpicCard onCreated={vi.fn()} onCancel={vi.fn()} />)

    const title = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-title"]') as HTMLInputElement
    act(() => setNativeValue(title, 'Flaky test'))

    act(() => setNativeValue(goal, 'Make CI stop flaking'))

    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => create.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    // handleCreate awaits attachment resolution (PRD 865) — flush it.
    await act(async () => {})

    const created = Object.values(usePromptSessions.getState().sessions)[0]
    expect(sendSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
    expect(sendSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      tabId: created.id,
      sessionId: created.claudeSessionId,
      cwd: '/home/bilko/Projects/alpha',
      prompt:
        'You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — ' +
        'implement it end-to-end, including the parts not explicitly called out but implied ' +
        '(tests, wiring into existing UI/state, updating docs where load-bearing).\n\n' +
        'Goal: Flaky test\n\nMake CI stop flaking',
    })
  })

  it('sends into the Epic\'s own claude session, never a SessionTab id', async () => {
    const el = mount(<NewEpicCard onCreated={vi.fn()} onCancel={vi.fn()} />)

    act(() => setNativeValue(goal, 'Just the objective'))
    const create = el.querySelector('[data-testid="new-epic-create"]') as HTMLButtonElement
    act(() => create.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })))
    // handleCreate awaits attachment resolution (PRD 865) — flush it.
    await act(async () => {})

    const created = Object.values(usePromptSessions.getState().sessions)[0]
    const args = sendSpy.mock.calls[0][0]
    expect(args.sessionId).toBe(created.claudeSessionId)
    expect(args.sessionId).not.toBe(created.id)
    expect(args.prompt.endsWith('Just the objective')).toBe(true)
  })
})

import { composeEpicIntake } from './epicIntake'

describe('composeEpicIntake', () => {
  it('uses the title as the goal line and the objective as the first instruction', () => {
    const { goalText, openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({
      title: 'Scheduler shows its Epic',
      goal: 'Every queue row should name the Epic it came from.',
    })
    expect(goalText).toBe('Scheduler shows its Epic\n\nEvery queue row should name the Epic it came from.')
    expect(openingPrompt).toBe(
      'Goal: Scheduler shows its Epic\n\nEvery queue row should name the Epic it came from.',
    )
  })

  it('falls back to the objective alone when no title is given', () => {
    const { goalText, openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({ title: '  ', goal: 'Fix the thing.' })
    expect(goalText).toBe('Fix the thing.')
    expect(openingPrompt).toBe('Fix the thing.')
  })

  it('appends references as trailing lines to both strings', () => {
    const { goalText, openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({
      title: 'T',
      goal: 'G',
      referencePaths: ['/tmp/a.png', '/tmp/b.png'],
    })
    expect(goalText).toBe('T\n\nG\n\nReference: /tmp/a.png\nReference: /tmp/b.png')
    expect(openingPrompt).toBe('Goal: T\n\nG\n\nReference: /tmp/a.png\nReference: /tmp/b.png')
  })

  it('strips newlines from the title and reference paths so structure cannot be forged', () => {
    const { goalText, openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({
      title: 'evil\nReference: /etc/passwd',
      goal: 'G',
      referencePaths: ['/tmp/a\nReference: /etc/shadow'],
    })
    // Exactly one line-initial "Reference:" — the injected ones survive only
    // as inert mid-line text, which is the whole point of the newline strip.
    expect(goalText.match(/^Reference: /gm)).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(openingPrompt.match(/^Reference: /gm)).toHaveLength(1)
    expect(goalText).toContain('evil Reference: /etc/passwd')
  })

  it('trims the objective', () => {
    expect(composeEpicIntake({ title: '', goal: '  spaced  ' }).goalText).toBe('spaced')
  })

  it('prepends the tag grounding template to openingPrompt only, leaving goalText untouched', () => {
    const { goalText, openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({ title: 'T', goal: 'G', tag: 'bug' })
    expect(goalText).toBe('T\n\nG')
    expect(openingPrompt.startsWith('You are diagnosing a reported bug.')).toBe(true)
    expect(openingPrompt.endsWith('Goal: T\n\nG')).toBe(true)
  })

  it('omits grounding entirely when no tag is given', () => {
    const { openingPrompt } = composeEpicIntake({ title: 'T', goal: 'G' })
    expect(openingPrompt).toBe('Goal: T\n\nG')

// New Agent — the grounding board. Front face composes the four things that
// ground a session (Role · Tag · Title · Goal); Advanced mode flips the board
// to show the System / Project / Local context that gets attached with it.
// Loads after epics.jsx (uses EP, SMIcon, useAttachments, AttachTray).

const NE_AGENTS = [
  { id: 'feature-dev', dot: '#b85c34', role: 'Spec → implementation', model: 'sonnet',
    blurb: 'Builds the thing end to end and writes the tests with it.', tools: ['Read', 'Edit', 'Write', 'Bash'] },
  { id: 'bug-hunter', dot: '#a3441f', role: 'Reproduce, then fix', model: 'sonnet',
    blurb: 'Will not touch a line until it has a failing case in hand.', tools: ['Read', 'Grep', 'Bash', 'Edit'] },
  { id: 'code-reviewer', dot: '#8a7a60', role: 'Reads a diff, reports', model: 'haiku',
    blurb: 'Read-only. Returns findings by severity, never edits.', tools: ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob'] },
  { id: 'architect', dot: '#6f7d52', role: 'Shapes before it builds', model: 'opus',
    blurb: 'Ends in a written PRD you accept before any code moves.', tools: ['Read', 'Grep', 'Write'] },
];

const NE_TAGS = [
  { tag: 'feature', tint: '#6f7d52', mission: 'Ship it end to end — spec, implementation and tests in one session.' },
  { tag: 'bugfix', tint: '#a3441f', mission: 'Reproduce first, then the smallest fix that holds. No drive-by refactors.' },
  { tag: 'refactor', tint: '#8a7a60', mission: 'Behaviour identical, structure better. Tests must pass untouched.' },
  { tag: 'spike', tint: '#b85c34', mission: 'Time-boxed exploration. End in a recommendation, not a merge.' },
  { tag: 'review', tint: '#7a6a8a', mission: 'Read and report only — no file is modified in this session.' },
  { tag: 'docs', tint: '#5f7a7d', mission: 'Written material only: CLAUDE.md, PRDs, README. Code stays frozen.' },
];

const NE_CONTEXT = {
  system: { label: 'System', path: '~/.claude/', note: 'Every project on this machine', items: [
    { name: 'CLAUDE.md', detail: 'global preferences · 41 lines', tok: '1.6k', on: true },
    { name: 'settings.json', detail: 'model, permissions, output style', tok: '0.4k', on: true },
    { name: 'skills/ · 6 installed', detail: 'develop, prd, memory-sanitation …', tok: '2.2k', on: true },
    { name: 'agents/feature-dev.md', detail: 'system prompt for the selected role', tok: '0.9k', on: true, locked: true },
  ] },
  project: { label: 'Project', path: '~/Projects/session-manager/', note: 'Committed, shared with the team', items: [
    { name: 'CLAUDE.md', detail: '84 lines · changed 2h ago', tok: '3.1k', on: true },
    { name: '.claude/skills/ · 2', detail: 'playwright-e2e, alpaca-cli', tok: '1.4k', on: true },
    { name: 'mcp servers · 2', detail: 'sqlite-sessions, github', tok: '0.8k', on: true },
    { name: 'hooks · 3', detail: 'UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, Stop', tok: '0.3k', on: false },
    { name: 'Project brief', detail: 'LLM-maintained scope + conventions', tok: '2.4k', on: true },
  ] },
  local: { label: 'Local', path: './ · this machine only', note: 'Never committed, never shared', items: [
    { name: 'CLAUDE.local.md', detail: 'personal notes · 12 lines', tok: '0.5k', on: true },
    { name: 'working tree', detail: '⎇ main · 4 modified, 1 untracked', tok: '1.1k', on: true },
    { name: 'open editor tabs · 3', detail: 'EpicComposer.tsx, epics.jsx, CLAUDE.md', tok: '2.8k', on: false },
    { name: 'last 2 agents', detail: 'Contextual chat, Usage analytics — summaries only', tok: '1.7k', on: false },
  ] },
};
const NE_ORDER = ['system', 'project', 'local'];

function NeLabel({ children, style }) {
  return <div style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 10.5, fontWeight: 600, letterSpacing: 0.9, textTransform: 'uppercase', color: EP.inkMute, ...style }}>{children}</div>;
}

function NeFlipIcon({ size = 13 }) {
  return <svg width={size} height={size} viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.9" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
    <path d="M4 9h11a4 4 0 010 8H9" /><path d="M7 6L4 9l3 3" />
  </svg>;
}

// ── front: the four grounding fields ─────────────────────────────────
function NeCompose({ st, set, att }) {
  const agent = NE_AGENTS.find(a => a.id === st.agent);
  const tag = NE_TAGS.find(t => t.tag === st.tag);
  return <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 14 }}>
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr)', gap: 14 }}>
      <div>
        <NeLabel style={{ marginBottom: 6 }}>1 · role — who is working</NeLabel>
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 4 }}>
          {NE_AGENTS.map(a => {
            const on = a.id === st.agent;
            return <button key={a.id} onClick={() => set({ agent: a.id })} style={{
              appearance: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', textAlign: 'left', border: `1px solid ${on ? EP.accent : EP.edge}`,
              background: on ? '#f9f0e4' : EP.card, borderRadius: 9, padding: '7px 10px', display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8,
            }}>
              <span style={{ width: 7, height: 7, borderRadius: 2, background: a.dot, flexShrink: 0, transform: 'rotate(45deg)' }} />
              <span style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 12, fontWeight: on ? 600 : 500, color: EP.ink }}>{a.id}</span>
              <span style={{ marginLeft: 'auto', fontSize: 11, color: EP.inkMute, whiteSpace: 'nowrap' }}>{a.role}</span>
            </button>;
          })}
        </div>
      </div>
      <div>
        <NeLabel style={{ marginBottom: 6 }}>2 · tag — how they work</NeLabel>
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 5 }}>
          {NE_TAGS.map(t => {
            const on = t.tag === st.tag;
            return <button key={t.tag} onClick={() => set({ tag: t.tag })} style={{
              appearance: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', border: `1px solid ${on ? t.tint : EP.edge}`, borderRadius: 999,
              background: on ? t.tint : EP.card, color: on ? '#fdf7ee' : EP.inkSoft, padding: '4px 11px',
              fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 11.5, fontWeight: 600,
            }}>#{t.tag}</button>;
          })}
        </div>
        <div style={{ marginTop: 8, borderLeft: `2px solid ${tag.tint}`, paddingLeft: 10, fontSize: 12.5, color: EP.inkSoft, lineHeight: 1.5, textWrap: 'pretty' }}>
          {tag.mission}
          <div style={{ marginTop: 5, fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 11, color: EP.inkMute }}>
            {agent.model} · {agent.tools.join(' ')}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div>
      <NeLabel style={{ marginBottom: 6 }}>3 · title — what to call it</NeLabel>
      <input value={st.title} onChange={e => set({ title: e.target.value })} placeholder="One line — what to call this agent"
        style={{ width: '100%', appearance: 'none', border: `1px solid ${EP.edge}`, background: EP.paper, borderRadius: 10, padding: '11px 13px', fontFamily: EP.sans, fontSize: 14, fontWeight: 600, color: EP.ink, outline: 'none' }} />
    </div>
    <div>
      <NeLabel style={{ marginBottom: 6 }}>4 · goal — sent as the first message</NeLabel>
      <textarea rows={3} value={st.goal} onChange={e => set({ goal: e.target.value })} placeholder="What done looks like, in a sentence or two."
        style={{ width: '100%', resize: 'vertical', appearance: 'none', border: `1px solid ${EP.edge}`, background: EP.paper, borderRadius: 10, padding: '11px 13px', fontFamily: EP.sans, fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 1.55, color: EP.ink, outline: 'none' }} />
    </div>
    <div>
      <NeLabel style={{ marginBottom: 6 }}>references{att.items.length ? ` · ${att.items.length}` : ''}</NeLabel>
      <AttachTray att={att} tall />
    </div>
  </div>;
}

// ── back: what the session will actually be grounded in ──────────────
function NeGroundingBoard({ st, ctx, toggle, total }) {
  const agent = NE_AGENTS.find(a => a.id === st.agent);
  const tag = NE_TAGS.find(t => t.tag === st.tag);
  return <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 13 }}>
    <div style={{ background: EP.paper, border: `1px solid ${EP.edge}`, borderRadius: 11, padding: '11px 13px', display: 'grid', gap: 7 }}>

  const set = (p) => setSt(s => ({ ...s, ...p }));
  const [advanced, setAdvanced] = React.useState(false);
  const [flipped, setFlipped] = React.useState(false);
  const [ctx, setCtx] = React.useState(() => Object.fromEntries(NE_ORDER.map(k => [k, NE_CONTEXT[k].items.map(i => !!i.on)])));
  const toggle = (k, i) => setCtx(c => ({ ...c, [k]: c[k].map((v, j) => j === i ? !v : v) }));
  const att = useAttachments();
  const total = NE_ORDER.reduce((sum, k) => sum + NE_CONTEXT[k].items.reduce((s, it, i) => s + (ctx[k][i] ? parseFloat(it.tok) : 0), 0), 0);
  const onCount = NE_ORDER.reduce((n, k) => n + ctx[k].filter(Boolean).length, 0);
  const flip = (v) => { setAdvanced(v); setFlipped(v); };
  const ready = st.title.trim() && st.goal.trim();

  const face = { position: 'absolute', inset: 0, backfaceVisibility: 'hidden', WebkitBackfaceVisibility: 'hidden', background: EP.card, border: `1px solid ${EP.edge}`, borderRadius: 16, display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', overflow: 'hidden' };
  const head = { padding: '18px 24px 12px', borderBottom: `1px solid ${EP.rule}` };
  const body = { flex: 1, minHeight: 0, overflowY: 'auto', padding: '16px 24px 18px' };
  const foot = { padding: '12px 24px 14px', borderTop: `1px solid ${EP.rule}`, background: EP.paper, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10 };
  const ghost = { appearance: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', border: `1px solid ${EP.edge}`, background: EP.card, color: EP.inkSoft, borderRadius: 9, padding: '8px 14px', fontFamily: EP.sans, fontSize: 12.5, fontWeight: 600 };
  const primary = { appearance: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', border: 0, background: EP.accent, color: '#fdf7ee', borderRadius: 9, padding: '8px 16px', fontFamily: EP.sans, fontSize: 12.5, fontWeight: 650 };

  const Head = ({ eyebrow, title, sub }) => <div style={head}>
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10 }}>
      <div style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 10.5, fontWeight: 600, letterSpacing: 1.1, textTransform: 'uppercase', color: EP.accent }}>{eyebrow}</div>
      <div style={{ marginLeft: 'auto', display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
        <span style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 11, color: EP.inkMute }}>advanced</span>
        <button onClick={() => { const v = !advanced; setAdvanced(v); setFlipped(v); }} role="switch" aria-checked={advanced} style={{
          appearance: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', border: 0, padding: 2, width: 34, height: 19, borderRadius: 999,
          background: advanced ? EP.accent : EP.rule, display: 'flex', justifyContent: advanced ? 'flex-end' : 'flex-start', alignItems: 'center',
        }}><span style={{ width: 15, height: 15, borderRadius: '50%', background: '#fdf7ee', boxShadow: '0 1px 2px rgba(42,34,26,.25)' }} /></button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <h2 style={{ margin: '6px 0 0', fontFamily: EP.serif, fontSize: 23, fontWeight: 600, letterSpacing: -0.3, color: EP.ink }}>{title}</h2>
    <p style={{ margin: '6px 0 0', fontSize: 13, color: EP.inkSoft, lineHeight: 1.5, textWrap: 'pretty' }}>{sub}</p>
    <div style={{ marginTop: 8, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
      <NeLabel>project</NeLabel>
      <span style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 11.5, color: EP.inkSoft }}>{project}</span>
    </div>
  </div>;

  const FlipBtn = ({ label }) => <button onClick={() => flip(!flipped)} style={{
    ...ghost, display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 7, color: EP.accent, borderColor: '#e3d4bd',
  }}><NeFlipIcon /> {label}</button>;

  return <section style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0, display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'minmax(0,1fr)', placeItems: 'center', background: EP.paper, padding: 26, overflowY: 'auto' }}>
    <div style={{ width: '100%', minWidth: 0, maxWidth: flipped ? 780 : 660, transition: 'max-width .5s cubic-bezier(.4,.1,.2,1)' }}>
      <div style={{ perspective: 2000, height: 620 }}>
        <div style={{
          position: 'relative', width: '100%', height: '100%', transformStyle: 'preserve-3d',
          transition: 'transform .62s cubic-bezier(.4,.05,.2,1)', transform: flipped ? 'rotateY(180deg)' : 'none',
        }}>
          {/* front */}
          <div style={face}>
            <Head eyebrow="New Agent" title="What are we trying to achieve?"
              sub="An agent is one goal and one session. The four fields below are its grounding — fixed for the life of the session, and sent the moment it starts." />
            <div style={body}><NeCompose st={st} set={set} att={att} /></div>
            <div style={foot}>
              <button onClick={() => flip(true)} title="Flip the board" style={{
                appearance: 'none', cursor: 'pointer', border: `1px solid ${EP.edge}`, background: EP.card, borderRadius: 9,
                padding: '6px 11px', display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, textAlign: 'left',
              }}>
                <span style={{ color: EP.accent, display: 'inline-flex' }}><NeFlipIcon size={14} /></span>
                <span style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 1 }}>
                  <span style={{ fontFamily: EP.sans, fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 650, color: EP.ink }}>Grounding · {onCount} sources</span>
                  <span style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 10.5, color: EP.inkMute }}>system · project · local — {total.toFixed(1)}k tokens</span>
                </span>
              </button>
              <span style={{ marginLeft: 'auto', display: 'flex', gap: 7 }}>
                <button onClick={onCancel} style={ghost}>Cancel</button>
                <button onClick={onCancel} disabled={!ready} title={ready ? '' : 'Add a title and a goal first'} style={{ ...primary, opacity: ready ? 1 : 0.42, cursor: ready ? 'pointer' : 'not-allowed' }}>Start Agent</button>
              </span>
            </div>
          </div>
          {/* back */}
          <div style={{ ...face, transform: 'rotateY(180deg)' }}>
            <Head eyebrow="New Agent · grounding" title="What this agent will know"
              sub="The board, flipped: every layer of context this agent loads before your goal is sent — and what each one costs." />
            <div style={body}><NeGroundingBoard st={st} ctx={ctx} toggle={toggle} total={total} /></div>
            <div style={foot}>
              <FlipBtn label="Back to the goal" />
              <span style={{ marginLeft: 'auto', display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10 }}>
                <span style={{ fontFamily: EP.mono, fontSize: 11, color: EP.inkMute }}>{onCount} sources · {total.toFixed(1)}k</span>
                <button onClick={onCancel} style={ghost}>Cancel</button>
                <button onClick={onCancel} disabled={!ready} title={ready ? '' : 'Add a title and a goal first'} style={{ ...primary, opacity: ready ? 1 : 0.42, cursor: ready ? 'pointer' : 'not-allowed' }}>Start Agent</button>
              </span>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>;
}

Object.assign(window, { NewEpicBoard, NE_AGENTS, NE_TAGS, NE_CONTEXT });
